_entry_shape._note: The shape every entry must carry, recorded here so it is visible before anyone has to invent it. All thirteen fields are required and each is checked on its own by `expansion_policy.entries_for`. `dimensions` is what makes a ratification cover a known divergence WITHOUT covering the document: a dimension not named here stays a reported divergence, so a new defect on a ratified document still shows.
_entry_shape.authorization_provenance: how the authorization reached the session that wrote the entry, and from whom -- never an implied direct interaction
dimensions: the gated dimensions this entry covers, and only these
_entry_shape.evidence: path to the committed measurement whose numbers these are

floors.<dimension>: the bound past which this becomes a regression again

_entry_shape.reason: the attributed cause, in enough detail to re-check

reference_at_record.<dimension>: the reference arm at the same measurement

_entry_shape.review_condition: what retires this entry, expressed so the stale rule enforces it

_note: The acceptance record for the EXPANSION corpus, kept deliberately separate from `parity_policy.json`. That file governs the gated 16 and pins `corpus_manifest.json`; this one governs the 29 expansion documents and pins `corpus_expansion.json`. An expansion finding written into the gated policy would be unreachable (adjudicate never sees a document outside the gated manifest, and parity_expansion.py refuses the waiver sections by design), falsely bound (it would carry `corpus_manifest_sha256` for a document that manifest does not contain), and cross-contaminating (one record for two corpora, so a re-record of either could not be told from the other). The reader in `testkit/expansion_policy.py` refuses to read either artifact as the other, in both directions. See docs/corpus-expansion.md section 2 for the separation this preserves, and section 7 for what promotion into the gate would require instead.
_what_this_does_not_do: It does not adjudicate. `parity_expansion.py` measures and never authorises, and applying an entry from this file annotates a measured row with `ratified: true` beside the verdict the measurement produced -- it never converts a verdict into a pass and never changes that module's exit code. What IS enforced is this file's own integrity: a moved corpus, a malformed section, an entry naming a document the corpus does not contain, a floor breached, a finding that stopped describing anything, or an entry no run measured are all errors, in the same class as a corpus that does not match its manifest.

corpus._note: Pinned by content, not by name. A corpus that has moved invalidates every floor measured over it, so the reader refuses rather than comparing against numbers that describe other bytes. Re-pinning means re-checking every entry, which is the point.
corpus.name: corpus_expansion.json

profiles._note: Keyed by the FULL profile ID of the run -- the named profile both arms share, with only the backend differing. The expansion corpus is measured at two, and a finding at one says nothing about the other: different renderer, different distribution, different numbers. Only the section matching the run is ever selected and nothing is borrowed across the boundary, which is the rule `backend_parity._policy_profile_errors` enforces for the gated policy, applied to a file that has to serve two profiles at once.
